newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen tribe hijacks minister's car, kidnaps driver.
newsitem.headline: Yemen tribe hijacks minister's car, kidnaps driver.

text.p: Tribesmen hijacked the car of Yemen's minister of agriculture and kidnapped his driver in the capital Sanaa on Saturday before releasing him hours later, a security source said.
Minister of Agriculture Ahmad Salem al-Jabali was not in the car, the source told Reuters.
"Tribesmen from the Jehim area in the Marib governorate hijacked the car and abducted the driver of the minister of agriculture," he said.
The driver was taken to the Jehim area, 170 km (105 miles) north of the capital, where he was later set free.

"They released the driver after beating him up," the source said, adding the driver was on his way back to Sanaa with security officials who found him walking back to Sanaa on foot. The tribesmen kept the car.
"The tribes apparently have illegal demands they want to have fulfilled by the minister. But he refused to do this," a Yemeni official said.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or foreigners working in Yemen for use as bargaining chips.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.
In January, members of a tribe kidnapped 17 elderly French tourists in the Marib governorate but released them later in the month.
The minister, who was at home in Sanaa at the time of the incident, is known to frequently drive alone, without a driver or security guards.
